newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador's Bucaram loses defense minister.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's Bucaram loses defense minister.

text.p: Embattled President Abdala Bucaram suffered another major setback in his fight for political survival on Saturday when his defence minister resigned, citing the army's professed neutrality in the face of Ecuador's three-day-old crisis.

The resignation of Gen. Victor Bayas followed that of three other cabinet officials in 48 hours, including Energy Minister Alfredo Adum, and left Bucaram looking very much alone at the top of his shaky six-month-old government.
It also came amid reports that the military had withdrawn all support for Bucaram.

Bayas did not refer to those reports in remarks to reporters at the defence ministry late on Saturday. But he said the military high command had agreed to maintain strict "neutrality" amid the political crisis, and that his closeness to Bucaram was seen as compromising that stance.
"I could no longer maintain the portfolio," said Bayas.

Bayas had declared a nationwide state of emergency on Friday in an unsuccessful bid to quell anti-Bucaram street protests in Quito and Guayaquil. An 18-year-old student was killed in clashes between riot police and demonstrators in the capital.

Bucaram, who left the heavy fortified presidential palace in Quito late on Friday for his traditional power base in Guayaquil, has dismissed Thursday's vote by Congress deposing him on grounds of mental incompetence as an attempted coup and said he had no intention of stepping down.

But national radio said he had lost all support from the military, which remains a potent force in the political life of this South American country despite having handed over power to a civilian government in 1979.
The high command is widely expected to have a hand in chosing Bucaram's possible successor and in ending the constitutional crisis tearing at the nation's seams.
"Bucaram no longer has the support of the military high command," Radio Quito said in news bulletin, citing what it said were sources close to senior military officials.
The report could not be immediately confirmed.

Three top politicians, including Bucaram who is popularly known as "El Loco" or "madman," have staked claims to the presidency since Thursday night. The other contenders are Vice President Rosalia Arteaga, who claims she is Bucaram's legal successor, and congressional leader Fabian Alarcon, who was named acting president by Congress.

Seeking to end the conflict, two of Ecuador's elder statesmen publicly endorsed calls by leading newspapers for all three of the country's current "presidents" to step aside in favour of a more neutral figure to be picked by national consensus.

El Comercio of Quito and El Universo of Guayaquil both said the constitutional crisis -- prompted by the fact that three people were simultaneously claiming to be president -- had created a power vacuum that could only lead to political bloodletting or a military dictatorship.

Former presidents Osvaldo Hurtado and Sixto Duran Ballen issued a joint statement agreeing with the newspapers and effectively urging the three pretenders to Ecuador's presidential throne to step aside for the good of their country.
